# Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)

> **Real programme record.** The facts below were checked against official Government of
> India pages on 2026-09-28. See [[SRC-001 — SISFS — Official Scheme Page]] and
> [[SRC-002 — SISFS — Frequently Asked Questions]].

## Overview

The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme provides financial assistance to DPIIT-recognised
startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and
commercialisation. It is administered by DPIIT, but the money is disbursed to startups
through eligible incubators across India, which is the practical gate on any application.

- **Provider:** [[ORG-001 — DPIIT — Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade]]
- **Country:** India
- **Type:** Fund

## Provider

[[ORG-001 — DPIIT — Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade]]

## What the benefit is

A two-tranche seed support package:

1. **Up to INR 20 lakh as a grant** for validating proof of concept, developing a prototype,
   or running product trials. Released in milestone-based instalments.
2. **Up to INR 50 lakh as investment** for market entry, commercialisation or scale-up,
   through convertible debentures or debt or debt-linked instruments.

Each tranche may be availed once. The fund may not be used for creating any facilities, and
must be spent on the purpose for which it was granted.

## Amount and currency

- Minimum: *(blank — the two tranches have separate ceilings, not a single published range)*
- Maximum: 5,000,000
- Currency: INR

## Who can apply

DPIIT-recognised startups incorporated not more than two years before application, with a
product or service idea showing market fit, viable commercialisation and scope of scaling,
and using technology in the core product or service, business model, distribution model or
methodology. The scheme is sector-agnostic, and no criterion may be waived.

### Eligibility criteria

- Recognised as a startup by DPIIT
- Incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application
- Business idea for a product or service with market fit, viable commercialisation and scope of scaling
- Uses technology in its core product or service, business model, distribution model or methodology
- Scheme is sector-agnostic, with no sector restriction
- All criteria must be met on the date the application is submitted, and no exemptions are available

### Exclusions

- Individual entrepreneurs; only DPIIT-recognised startups may apply
- Startups that have already availed the grant tranche or the debt or convertible debenture tranche
- Use of the seed fund for creation of any facilities, or for any purpose other than the one it was granted for

Per-company eligibility assessments belong in a Match record, not in this note.

## Key dates

| Date | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Application opens | *(blank — open year-round)* |
| Application deadline | *(blank — open year-round)* |
| Deadline type | Rolling |
| Last verified | 2026-09-28 |

## Matching funds

No matching or cost-share requirement is published for this scheme.

## How to apply

- Application URL: https://seedfund.startupindia.gov.in/
- Method: Online application using the DPIIT recognition login, routed through a chosen eligible incubator. Up to three incubators may be applied to simultaneously. Applications are open year-round and free of cost.

## Source

- Source URL: https://seedfund.startupindia.gov.in/
- Supporting sources: [[SRC-001 — SISFS — Official Scheme Page]], [[SRC-002 — SISFS — Frequently Asked Questions]]

## Notes

Launched 19 April 2021. The scheme outlay of INR 945 crore is published on the Government of
India ISTI portal rather than on the scheme page recorded here, so it is not carried in
this record's fields. The scheme page is JavaScript-rendered; its wording was obtained
through indexed extracts of the same official URL and is consistent with the FAQ page.

# Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)

> **Real programme record, verification incomplete.** The programme is real. The figures
> below come from official Ministry of MSME pages, but two of those pages disagree on the
> maximum admissible project cost, so this record is marked `Needs review`. Checked
> 2026-09-28. See [[SRC-003 — PMEGP — Ministry of MSME Scheme Page]] and
> [[SRC-004 — PMEGP — Official Programme Portal]].

## Overview

PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy programme that helps individuals set up new micro-enterprises
in the non-farm sector. The Government of India provides a margin money subsidy, and a bank
provides the balance as term loan and working capital. KVIC is the national nodal agency and
routes the subsidy to the beneficiary's bank account.

- **Provider:** [[ORG-002 — KVIC — Khadi and Village Industries Commission]]
- **Country:** India
- **Type:** Subsidy

## Provider

[[ORG-002 — KVIC — Khadi and Village Industries Commission]]

## What the benefit is

A percentage margin money subsidy on the admissible project cost, not a fixed award. The
bank finances the balance, and the beneficiary puts in a contribution of 10% (general
category) or 5% (special category) of project cost.

| Category | Area | Beneficiary contribution | Subsidy rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| General category | Urban | 10% | 15% |
| General category | Rural | 10% | 25% |
| Special category | Urban | 5% | 25% |
| Special category | Rural | 5% | 35% |

Special category covers SC, ST, OBC, minorities, women, ex-servicemen, transgender persons,
differently abled persons, NER, aspirational districts, and hill and border areas as notified
by the Government.

## Amount and currency

- Minimum: *(blank — the subsidy is a percentage, not a fixed sum)*
- Maximum: *(blank — the published ceilings are on project cost, not on the award; project cost caps are recorded under eligibility criteria)*
- Currency: INR

## Who can apply

Any individual above 18 years of age. The scheme covers the non-farm sector in both
manufacturing and business or services. Only new projects are considered.

### Eligibility criteria

- Applicant is an individual above 18 years of age
- Project is a new micro-enterprise in the non-farm sector; only new projects are considered
- Minimum VIII standard pass for manufacturing projects costing above INR 10 lakh and business or service projects costing above INR 5 lakh
- Maximum admissible project cost of INR 50 lakh in manufacturing and INR 20 lakh in business or service
- Beneficiary contribution of 10% of project cost for the general category and 5% for the special category
- Subsidy rate of 15% urban and 25% rural for the general category, and 25% urban and 35% rural for the special category
- Rural classification of the project location determines the applicable subsidy rate
- A second loan is available for upgradation of existing PMEGP, REGP or MUDRA units

### Exclusions

- Existing units set up under PMRY, REGP or any other Government of India or State Government scheme are not eligible for a first loan
- Units that have already availed a government subsidy under any other Government of India or State Government scheme are not eligible
- The scheme covers the non-farm sector only

Per-company eligibility assessments belong in a Match record, not in this note.

## Key dates

| Date | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Application opens | *(blank — not published)* |
| Application deadline | *(blank — not published)* |
| Deadline type | Unknown |
| Last verified | 2026-09-28 |

The official page describes applications being invited through advertisements by the state
and divisional KVIC directors in consultation with the KVIB and the Director of Industries.
No closing date is published, which is why `deadline_type` is `Unknown` rather than
`Rolling`.

## Matching funds

Yes. The beneficiary contributes 10% (general) or 5% (special) of project cost from their
own funds, and the bank finances the remaining balance as term loan and working capital.

## How to apply

- Application URL: https://pmegp.msme.gov.in/
- Method: Online through the Ministry of MSME PMEGP portal, or through the State KVIC Directorate, State KVIB or District Industries Centre, with a detailed project report. A recommendation from the competent authority is required, and sanction is subject to bank approval and availability of funds.

## Source

- Source URL: https://www.msme.gov.in/1-prime-ministers-employment-generation-programme-pmegp
- Supporting sources: [[SRC-003 — PMEGP — Ministry of MSME Scheme Page]], [[SRC-004 — PMEGP — Official Programme Portal]]

## Notes

**Unresolved discrepancy.** Other official Ministry of MSME pages give lower maximum
admissible project costs of INR 25 lakh for manufacturing and INR 10 lakh for business or
service. Those pages are not recorded as separate sources here. Until the conflict is
settled against the current scheme guidelines, do not rely on a specific project cost
ceiling, and keep this record at `Needs review`.

# Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)

> **Real programme record.** The facts below were read directly from the official USDA Rural
> Development programme page on 2026-09-28. See
> [[SRC-005 — REAP — USDA Rural Development Programme Page]].

## Overview

REAP helps agricultural producers and rural small businesses install renewable energy systems
and make energy efficiency improvements, through grants, guaranteed loans, or both combined.
It is administered by USDA Rural Development under 7 CFR Part 4280 and 7 CFR 5001.

- **Provider:** [[ORG-003 — USDA Rural Development]]
- **Country:** USA
- **Type:** Grant

## Provider

[[ORG-003 — USDA Rural Development]]

## What the benefit is

Three routes, in the programme's own terms:

- **Grants** of up to 50% of total eligible project costs
- **Loan guarantees** on loans of up to 75% of total eligible project costs
- **Combined** grant and loan guarantee funding of up to 75%

Eligible systems include biomass, geothermal, hydropower below 30 megawatts, hydrogen, small
and large wind, small and large solar, and ocean generation. Eligible efficiency improvements
include HVAC, insulation, lighting, cooling or refrigeration units, doors and windows, and
replacement of energy-inefficient equipment.

## Amount and currency

- Minimum: 1,500
- Maximum: 1,000,000
- Currency: USD

The published grant tiers are:

| Grant type | Minimum | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Renewable Energy System | 2,500 | 1,000,000 |
| Energy Efficiency Improvement | 1,500 | 500,000 |

The figures above are the outer bounds of both tiers.

## Who can apply

Agricultural producers, and small businesses in eligible rural areas. A small business must be
a private for-profit entity, a cooperative, an electric utility, or a Tribal corporation or
Tribal business entity, and must meet SBA size standards.

### Eligibility criteria

- Agricultural producer with at least 50% of gross income derived from agricultural operations
- Small business located in an eligible rural area, meaning a population of 50,000 residents or less
- Small business must be a private for-profit entity, a cooperative, an electric utility, or a Tribal corporation or Tribal business entity
- Must meet the Small Business Administration size standards in accordance with 13 CFR 121
- No outstanding delinquent federal taxes, debt, judgment or debarment
- Project must have technical merit and must use commercially available technology
- Energy Efficiency Improvement applications must contain a compliant energy audit or energy assessment
- All projects require an environmental review before award or construction

### Exclusions

- Projects located in areas with populations above 50,000, except that agricultural producers may place projects in non-rural areas where the project is associated with an on-site production operation
- Ineligible project costs including used equipment, vehicles, residential improvements, application preparation, lease payments, agricultural tillage equipment and subordinated owner debt
- Guaranteed loan funds are limited to certain purposes, with land acquisition, working capital, energy audits and assessments, and debt refinancing subject to further limitations

> Per-company eligibility assessments belong in a Match record, not in this note. No Match
> record has been created against this opportunity yet.

## Key dates

| Date | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Application opens | *(blank — applications accepted year-round)* |
| Application deadline | *(blank — applications accepted year-round)* |
| Deadline type | Rolling |
| Last verified | 2026-09-28 |

## Matching funds

Yes. Matching funds are required if applying for a grant only, and at least 25% of the project
cost must be provided if applying for a loan.

## How to apply

- Application URL: https://www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/rural-energy-america-program-renewable-energy-systems-energy-efficiency
- Method: Year-round applications through the local USDA Rural Development office; contact the State Rural Development Energy Coordinator for guidance.

## Source

- Source URL: https://www.rd.usda.gov/programs-services/rural-energy-america-program-renewable-energy-systems-energy-efficiency
- Supporting source: [[SRC-005 — REAP — USDA Rural Development Programme Page]]

## Notes

The 50% federal grant share is not automatic. It is reserved for zero-emission renewable
energy systems, projects in an Energy Community, energy efficiency improvements, and eligible
Tribal projects. Everything else is capped at 25%. The official page also notes that
citations may be subject to change, so check the governing regulations for a live
application. Older USDA publications showing USD 500,000 and USD 250,000 maximums predate
the Inflation Reduction Act and should not be relied on.

frontmatter.opportunity_name: Federal Research and Experimental Tax Credit (IRC Section 41)
frontmatter.description: A federal tax credit for taxpayers carrying on a trade or business that incur qualified research expenses, with a payroll tax credit option for qualified small businesses that have little or no income tax liability. The credit is claimed on the tax return rather than applied for from a funder.
company_stage: Qualified small business for the payroll tax credit option
beneficiary_type: Taxpayer carrying on a trade or business
Qualified small business for the payroll tax credit option
benefit_type: Payroll tax credit against employer social security and Medicare tax
frontmatter.benefit_description: The research credit is generally 20% of the excess of qualified research expenses for the taxable year over the base amount. Taxpayers may elect the alternative simplified credit under IRC 41(c)(4), equal to 14% of qualified research expenses over 50% of the average qualified research expenses for the three preceding taxable years. The credit is computed on Form 6765. A qualified small business may elect under IRC 41(h) and 3111(f) to apply part of the credit against its employer share of social security tax and, from 2023, its employer share of Medicare tax. The maximum research credit that may be elected for a tax year to be applied toward payroll taxes is USD 500,000 for tax years beginning after 31 December 2022, raised from USD 250,000 by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. amount_max records that payroll tax cap only; the general credit has no equivalent single cap in the recorded source.
frontmatter.eligibility_summary: Available to taxpayers that carry on a trade or business and incur qualified research expenses, with no sector restriction. A qualified small business may elect the payroll tax credit against employer social security and Medicare tax, which is designed for a business with little or no income tax liability. There is no funder to apply to and no closing date; the credit is claimed on the federal tax return.
eligibility_criteria: Taxpayer carries on a trade or business
Expenditures are treated as domestic research or experimental expenditures under section 174A
Research is technological in nature and its application is intended to be useful in the development of a new or improved business component
Substantially all of the activities constitute elements of a process of experimentation
For the payroll tax option, the taxpayer is a qualified small business
The election is made by completing the appropriate portion of Form 6765 and attaching it to a timely filed income tax return
Form 8974 must be completed and attached to the employment tax return to claim the payroll tax credit
exclusions: The payroll tax credit election cannot be made on an amended return
A payroll tax credit in excess of the employer share of social security and Medicare tax shown on the employment tax return is carried forward to the next period rather than refunded
Qualified research consortium payments are subject to separate rules under IRC 41(e) and are not covered by this record
frontmatter.application_method: Not a grant application. The credit is claimed on the federal tax return. Complete Form 6765 to make the payroll tax election and attach it to a timely filed, including extended, income tax return. Claim the credit by completing Form 8974 and attaching it to the employment tax return, for example Form 941. The credit is first used against employer social security tax up to USD 250,000 per quarter, then against employer Medicare tax, with any excess carried forward. Interim guidance on eligibility and the election is at Notice 2017-23.
frontmatter.notes: Read directly from the official IRS page on 2026-09-28; the page states it was last reviewed or updated 28-Jun-2026. See SRC-006. The recorded source does not state the gross receipts or gross income thresholds that determine qualified small business status, so those figures are deliberately left unconfirmed and must be taken from IRC 41(h) and Notice 2017-23 before any claim is planned. The limitation of the credit by taxable income as part of the general business credit appears in Congressional Research Service material rather than on this page, so it is not asserted as a criterion here. This is a tax measure, not a procurement or tender opportunity. The relevant date is the tax filing deadline, which the scheme does not fix, so deadline_type is Recurring rather than Fixed.

# Federal Research and Experimental Tax Credit (IRC Section 41)

> **Real programme record.** The facts below were read directly from the official IRS page
> on 2026-09-28, a page which states it was last reviewed or updated 28-Jun-2026. See
> [[SRC-006 — IRS — Qualified Small Business Payroll Tax Credit Page]].

## Overview

IRC Section 41 gives a credit against income tax for increasing research activities. A
qualified small business may elect to apply part of that credit against its payroll taxes,
which is the option intended for a startup with little or no income tax liability.

This is **not** a grant. There is no funder, no panel and no application decision. The
benefit is claimed on the tax return.

- **Provider:** [[ORG-004 — IRS — Internal Revenue Service]]
- **Country:** USA
- **Type:** Incentive

## Provider

[[ORG-004 — IRS — Internal Revenue Service]]

## What the benefit is

A credit, not a payment. Two calculations are available:

- **Regular credit:** 20% of the excess of qualified research expenses over the base amount
- **Alternative simplified credit (ASC):** 14% of qualified research expenses over 50% of the
  average qualified research expenses for the three preceding taxable years

A qualified small business may apply part of the credit against employer social security tax
and employer Medicare tax. The payroll tax credit is used first against employer social
security tax up to USD 250,000 per quarter, then against employer Medicare tax, and any
excess carries forward to the next quarter.

## Amount and currency

- Minimum: *(blank — the credit is a percentage of expenditure, not a fixed award)*
- Maximum: 500,000
- Currency: USD

`amount_max` records only the cap on the **payroll tax credit** that a qualified small
business may elect for a tax year — USD 500,000 for tax years beginning after 31 December
2022, raised from USD 250,000 by the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. The recorded source
gives no single equivalent cap for the general credit.

## Who can apply

Any taxpayer carrying on a trade or business that incurs qualified research expenses. There is
no sector restriction. The payroll tax option is limited to qualified small businesses.

### Eligibility criteria

- Taxpayer carries on a trade or business
- Expenditures are treated as domestic research or experimental expenditures under section 174A
- Research is technological in nature and its application is intended to be useful in the development of a new or improved business component
- Substantially all of the activities constitute elements of a process of experimentation
- For the payroll tax option, the taxpayer is a qualified small business
- The election is made by completing the appropriate portion of Form 6765 and attaching it to a timely filed income tax return
- Form 8974 must be completed and attached to the employment tax return to claim the payroll tax credit

### Exclusions

- The payroll tax credit election cannot be made on an amended return
- A payroll tax credit in excess of the employer share of social security and Medicare tax shown on the employment tax return is carried forward to the next period rather than refunded
- Qualified research consortium payments are subject to separate rules under IRC 41(e) and are not covered by this record

Per-company eligibility assessments belong in a Match record, not in this note.

## Key dates

| Date | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Application opens | *(blank — no application window)* |
| Application deadline | *(blank — the scheme fixes no date; the tax filing deadline applies)* |
| Deadline type | Recurring |
| Last verified | 2026-09-28 |

## Matching funds

None. A tax credit is not a cost-share programme.

## How to apply

- Application URL: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/qualified-small-business-payroll-tax-credit-for-increasing-research-activities
- Method: Claimed on the tax return, not applied for. Complete Form 6765 to make the payroll tax election and attach it to a timely filed return, then complete Form 8974 and attach it to the employment tax return. Interim guidance is at Notice 2017-23.

## Source

- Source URL: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/qualified-small-business-payroll-tax-credit-for-increasing-research-activities
- Supporting source: [[SRC-006 — IRS — Qualified Small Business Payroll Tax Credit Page]]

## Notes

The gross receipts and gross income thresholds that determine qualified small business status
are **not** stated on the recorded IRS page. They are deliberately left unconfirmed here and
must be taken from IRC 41(h) and Notice 2017-23 before any claim is planned. Section 174A
treatment of domestic research or experimental expenditures also affects the outcome and is
governed by recent guidance that changes over time.

## Pair

- Company: [[COMP-001 — DEMO — AgriSolar Systems Private Limited]]
- Opportunity: [[OPP-001 — Startup India Seed Fund Scheme — SISFS]]

## Assessment summary

The substantive fit looked reasonable. The company is a technology incorporation, the scheme
places no sector restriction, and a private limited company is an accepted form.

**It nonetheless fails on timing, permanently.** The scheme admits startups incorporated not
more than two years before the date of application. This company was incorporated on
2024-03-18, so that window closed on **2026-03-18**. As at 2026-09-28 the company is **924
days** old against a **730-day** limit: the window shut 194 days ago.

The test is measured at the date of application, and application dates only move forward. So
no application made from today onward can satisfy it. This is not a question waiting on an
application date, and no new information can rescue it. The pairing is `Ineligible` on this
criterion alone.

Recognition is separately unrecorded, and would still have been a mandatory precondition. It
is no longer the decisive question, because the date test fails on its own.

## Criteria met

- Private limited company, one of the incorporation forms recognised for DPIIT startup recognition
- Technology is used in the core product, which is the relevant test
- Scheme is sector-agnostic, so agricultural technology and renewable energy are not excluded
- Business activity has a plausible product with a scaling path, consistent with the market-fit criterion

## Criteria not met

- **Incorporation date.** Incorporated on 2024-03-18, which is not within two years of the
  application date. The two-year window closed on 2026-03-18; at 2026-09-28 the company is 924
  days old against a 730-day limit. No future application date can satisfy the test.

## Missing information

- Whether the company holds current DPIIT startup recognition, which is a mandatory
  precondition. Still unrecorded, but no longer decisive, because the incorporation-date
  criterion already fails on its own.

The following were also outstanding against this scheme. They are preserved because they
remain accurate statements of what the scheme requires, but they are now moot: no application
will be made, so none of them is being sought.

- Which eligible incubator would host an application, since support is disbursed through an incubator and the incubator applies its own selection
- Whether support would be sought as the grant tranche, the investment tranche, or both
- Current funding history, which would be needed to confirm neither tranche has already been availed
- A stated market-fit and commercialisation case, which the scheme requires and which is not recorded on the company profile

FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION. Rules read from [[SRC-001 — SISFS — Official Scheme Page]] and
cross-checked against [[SRC-002 — SISFS — Frequently Asked Questions]]. The two sources agree
on every point they share, including the not-more-than-two-years incorporation test. The
`Ineligible` conclusion rests on arithmetic applied to the company's own recorded founding
date against that published test, so it does not depend on the unresolved recognition
question. Company facts are invented.

## Notes

This pairing is the clearest example in the sample data of a date test being got wrong and then
corrected. The scheme measures the two-year incorporation window at the date of application,
which made the criterion look permanently provisional: it would have passed in February 2026
and failed from March 2026 onwards. Recorded against an as-of date of 2026-09-28, that window

further away. The criterion therefore belongs in `criteria_not_met` and the pairing is

date-sensitive criterion must be tested against a stated date and recorded as a positive only
while it is actually true. "Close to the boundary" is not a pass, and "the answer moves with
the calendar" only holds while some future date could still satisfy the test. Once the window
has closed, the question is answered, and the answer is no.

# DEMO — Rooftop Solar Installation — Works Framework

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE.**
> This tender does not exist. The buyer is a fictional body, the reference number is
> invented, and the URL uses a reserved domain that cannot resolve. It exists so the Notice
> record type can be exercised end to end without inventing a real government tender.

## What this record is for

A Notice is the buyer's published solicitation. It answers: what is being bought, who is
buying, what must a bidder satisfy, what must a bidder hand in, and by when.

It is deliberately **not**:

- a **Bid** — no company has decided to bid here. That is a separate record type.
- a **Contract** — nothing has been awarded.
- a funding **Opportunity** — this is a buyer with money to spend, not a funder with money
  to give. The two domains are not linked.

## What the buyer demands

`bid_security_required` and `bid_security_amount` are what the **buyer** demands from any
bidder. They say nothing about what any company has posted. When the bid record type arrives,
it will carry `security_posted_amount` for our own position, and the two must never be
confused.

`mandatory_bid_documents` lists what the tender requires from **every** bidder. It is not a
checklist of what one company has completed; that belongs on a bid record as
`completed_documents`.

## The two blank preference fields

`msme_or_small_business_preference` and `local_content_preference` are blank on purpose. These
are the two fields whose rules differ by country, and Phase 1 recorded both as needing
research that has not happened. A blank says "the notice does not establish this". Filling
them with plausible-sounding values would mean inventing procurement rules.

## Why the time of day matters

`bid_submission_deadline` is `2026-09-23` and `bid_submission_datetime` is
`2026-09-23 17:00 IST`. Both are recorded because a tender that closes at 17:00 is not the
same tender as one that closes at 09:00, and reading the date alone loses the distinction
that causes a missed bid. The importer requires the date part of the timestamp to match the
deadline.

## Evidence

`linked_sources` is empty. For a real notice this would hold the notice document and every
corrigendum, because the Source is the evidence and this record is only our current
understanding of it. A synthetic notice has no real document to link, and inventing a source
record to stand in for one would be the same fabrication in a different place.

# DEMO — Water-Quality Data Analysis Services — Multi Lot

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE.**
> This tender does not exist. It was written to exercise the multi-lot and amended paths in
> the schema, not to describe any real procurement.

## Why this record exists

Three properties are hard to see in a single demonstration record, so this one carries them:

**It is multi-lot.** `lot_structure` is `Multi lot` with `number_of_lots: 3`, and each lot is
bought separately. The importer rejects a contradiction here — three lots cannot be described
as `Single lot`, and `Multi lot` cannot mean one.

**It has been amended twice.** Corrigenda are the reason `amendment_count`,
`last_amended_date`, and `last_verified` exist at all. A corrigendum is a source document, so
in a real notice each one would be a Source record appended to `linked_sources`. The number
and date on this record exist to make staleness visible at a glance: an amended notice that
has not been re-read is the failure mode this catches.

Because `last_amended_date` is set, `last_verified` must be on or after it. Here it is
2026-08-10 against an amendment on 2026-08-08, so the check passes. The importer fails the
import if someone records an amendment and then leaves `last_verified` blank or earlier,
because that means the notice has not been re-read since it changed.

**It has closed.** `notice_status` is `Closed` and `number_of_bids_received` is 7, which is
only knowable after the opening. On `RFB-001` the same field is blank, because before an
opening the honest value is "not published" rather than `0`.

## A blank that means something

`bid_submission_datetime` is blank here even though `bid_submission_deadline` is not. This
fictional notice states a closing date and no time. Entering `00:00` would invent a cutoff
that nobody stated, and a wrong cutoff is exactly the error this field exists to prevent.

# DEMO — Pump Station Rehabilitation — Single Source

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE.**
> This tender does not exist. It exists to show that the schema handles a notice that says
> very little, without the importer inventing anything to fill the gaps.

## The sparsest useful case

`RFB-001` is a fully specified competitive tender and `RFB-002` is a multi-lot amended one.
This record is the opposite: a single-source award, where most of the timeline genuinely does
not apply.

| Field | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue_date` | `2026-06-15` | The notice was still issued. |
| `bid_submission_deadline` | blank | Nobody competes, so nothing is submitted. |
| `bid_opening_date` | blank | No bids are opened. |
| `deadline_type` | `Unknown` | There is no closing date to be fixed or rolling. |
| `evaluation_method` | `Not stated` | Nothing is evaluated against competitors. |

Every one of those blanks is a real property of a single-source procurement, not missing data
that the importer should have filled in. The importer never fills anything: it reports a
mismatch and stops.

## Blank is not zero

`number_of_bids_received` and `amendment_count` are blank, not `0`.

- Blank means **not published or not established**.
- `0` would mean **we know there were none**.

Those are different claims. On a single-source award the honest answer is "not applicable",
which the vault records as blank. `number_of_bids_received` carries the same warning in the
data dictionary because on a competitive notice it is usually unknown until the opening, and a
tempting `0` there would silently become a real number in a report.

## Currency is never summed

`estimated_value` is `1250000` and `estimated_value_currency` is `INR`, on separate fields
and always together. The importer fails any notice that states a value without its currency,
because a total across mixed currencies is a meaningless number that looks like a real one.

# DEMO — AgriSolar submission on RFB-001

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL BID.**
> No procurement was pursued, submitted, or awarded to produce this record.

## The most complete of the four

`RFB-001` is the fully specified competitive demonstration tender, so this is the
record that exercises most of the schema at once: a single lot, a real
submission with a time of day, security we posted, a partially completed document
checklist, and scores that are blank because the demonstration opening has not
happened yet.

| Field | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lot_numbers` | `[]` | `RFB-001` is `Single lot`, so naming a lot would be an error. |
| `bid_status` | `Submitted` | The demonstration portal accepted the bid on 2026-09-22. |
| `bid_submission_datetime` | `2026-09-22 16:40 IST` | The portal receipt showed a time and a zone, so both are recorded. |
| `security_posted_amount` | `96000 INR` | **We** posted this. `RFB-001.bid_security_amount` is what the buyer demands; the figures coincide because the demand was met, not because the fields mean the same thing. |
| `eligibility_status` | `Potentially eligible` | See below. |
| `technical_score` | blank | Scores are published only after an opening. Blank means not published, never `0`. |

## Why not `Eligible—verified`

The review happened — `reviewed_by` and `review_date` are recorded — but the
electrical contractor registration certificate is not filed, and
`evidence_sources` is empty. So the record stops at `Potentially eligible`.

This is the honest state, and it is what the importer's rule 5 exists to protect.
Claiming `Eligible—verified` here would mean asserting a real-world
qualification on the strength of prose that cannot be checked against anything,
and the gate would reject it: `evidence_notes` and `evidence_sources` are both
blank. The criteria that do appear met are recorded in `criteria_met`; the one
that is missing is recorded in `missing_information`. Nothing is quietly dropped.

`evidence_sources` is empty rather than pointing at a plausible-looking document
because every Source in this vault is real funding evidence. Linking a real
funding document here would assert that it evidenced a procurement qualification.
It did not.

## The document checklist is ours

`required_documents` repeats the notice's `mandatory_bid_documents` **plus** one
item we added for ourselves, and `completed_documents` is missing only that last
item. The subset rule passes because the three completed entries all appear in
the required list; the outstanding certification is the honest gap that keeps this
bid at `Potentially eligible`.

Note that the buyer's list and our list are not the same field. One is what the
tender demands of any bidder, the other is what this submission has ready.

## The three axes disagree, deliberately

`Potentially eligible` + `Bid` + `Submitted` reads oddly if you expect one
verdict. It is correct: we may or may not qualify, we chose to bid, and the bid
is in. Collapsing these into a single "bid status" would hide exactly the
question still open — whether we qualify — which is the one a reader needs.

## Deadline

Submitted 2026-09-22 at 16:40 IST against a 2026-09-23 17:00 IST cutoff: on
time, with about 24 hours 20 minutes of margin — the submission landed the
previous day, not 20 minutes before closing. `bid_status` may therefore be
`Submitted`. Had
the submission landed after that cutoff, the only honest values would have been
`Withdrawn` or `Not awarded` — rule 7 rejects a late bid that still claims to be
submitted.

`RFB-002` states `number_of_bids_received: 7`. This record is one of the seven.
Keeping the bids that did not win is the point of the module: without them a
notice's history reads as a list of successes, and the record cannot answer
whether we are improving.

A no-win record also carries the information that is expensive to reconstruct
later — which lots we actually bid on, and why we left the third one alone.

## Partial lot coverage

| Field | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lot_numbers` | `Lot 1`, `Lot 2` | `RFB-002` is `Multi lot` with three lots, so the list must be non-empty. It is also allowed to be a **subset**: we bid on two of the three. |
| `pre_bid_attended` | `false` | `RFB-002` states no pre-bid meeting, so there was nothing to attend. |
| `bid_status` | `Not awarded` | Submitted on time and lost. |

The biconditional in rule 2 has two directions and both matter here. An empty
`lot_numbers` on a multi-lot notice would make "which lot did we win?"
unanswerable. Naming lots on a single-lot notice is simply an error. This record
satisfies both directions at once, and `BID-001` satisfies the single-lot side.

`security_posted_status` is `Not required` because `RFB-002` states
`bid_security_required: false`. Both amount fields are blank rather than `0`,
because no security was posted and `0` would assert a posted instrument worth
nothing.

This is the counterpart to `BID-001`, where the same fields carry a real figure.
Same three fields, opposite situations — which is exactly why they are named
`security_posted_*` rather than reusing the notice's `bid_security_*`.

## Scores are visible here but not on BID-001

`BID-001` has blank scores because its opening has not happened. This record has
scores because the demonstration opening has. Both are blank-or-real according to
what is actually published; neither is `0` to mean "unknown".

`contract_basis` explains an award that happened **without** a competing bid.
There was no award here at all, so it is blank. The same is true on `BID-004`,
which won a genuinely competitive lot: on a competitive award the blank is the
correct value, not a missing one.

# DEMO — AgriSolar assessment of RFB-003

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL BID.**
> No procurement was pursued, submitted, or awarded to produce this record.

## The most important record in the folder

This is the bid that was never made, and it exists because a missing Bid record
cannot be told apart from an oversight. Six months from now someone will see
`RFB-003` on the demo list and ask whether we looked at it. This record answers
that, and answers it in one line: **we looked, and we declined.**

`bid_decision: No bid` with a dated rationale is the durable artefact. The
alternative — leaving no record — looks identical to having missed the notice.

## `Needs more information` is not `Ineligible`, and not `Potentially eligible`

`RFB-003` states no `eligibility_criteria` at all. That is a genuinely
indeterminate starting position: there is nothing to assess against, which is not
the same as failing an assessment.

| Value | Would mean |
| --- | --- |
| `Eligible—verified` | We checked the stated criteria against evidence. There are no stated criteria. |
| `Potentially eligible` | Nothing rules us out yet. |
| `Ineligible` | We checked and failed. |
| **`Needs more information`** | **There is nothing to check against. This is the record's answer.** |

The scope mismatch is recorded separately in `criteria_not_met`, because it is a
different kind of fact: a demonstrated absence rather than a missing document.
Keeping the two apart is what stops a later reader from concluding the company was
formally disqualified when it was simply the wrong work.

`reviewed_by` and `review_date` are blank here, unlike `BID-001`. A desk decision
was taken, but a formal eligibility review was never opened — and recording that
honestly is better than back-filling a reviewer to make the row look complete.

## The lifecycle stops at `Researching`

`bid_status` is `Researching`, not a terminal value. There is no
`Did not bid` lifecycle state, and there should not be one: the decision to
decline is `bid_decision`, while the lifecycle describes what happened to a bid we
actually made. Nothing was ever submitted, so nothing progressed. Inventing a
terminal state would collapse the two axes this module works hardest to keep
apart.

## Every submission field is blank, and all of them must be

`bid_submission_date`, `bid_submission_datetime`, and
`bid_submission_reference` are blank because no submission exists. This is the
case rule 6 protects: had `bid_status` been `Submitted`, those blanks would be a
validation failure. Note also that `RFB-003` publishes no
`bid_submission_deadline` at all, so there would be nothing to submit against.

`security_posted_status` is `Not required` rather than `Not submitted`, following
the notice, which demands no security. The distinction matters: "not required" is
a fact about the tender, "not submitted" would be a gap in our own work.

`BID-004` won a single lot, which cannot show what happens when an award covers
more than one. This record closes that gap:

| Bid | Company | Lots bid | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BID-002` | `COMP-002` | Lot 1, Lot 2 | Not awarded |
| `BID-004` | `COMP-003` | Lot 2 | Awarded — Lot 2 |
| `BID-005` | `COMP-001` | Lot 1, Lot 3 | **Awarded — Lot 1 and Lot 3** |

The award splits cleanly along the kind of work. `BID-004` took Lot 2, the
statistical-analysis lot, because that company has a water laboratory. This
company took Lots 1 and 3, the site and installation lots, because that is the
work it does. `BID-002` bid across that dividing line and lost both sides of it.

Because one award covers two lots, it produces two contract records — `CON-002`
for Lot 1 and `CON-003` for Lot 3. Both point back at this single bid. A
one-contract-per-bid model would have had to drop a lot or invent a second
award, which is why the relationship is one bid to many contracts.

## `awarded_lot` is blank, and it has to be

This is the one field on the record that a reader will expect to be filled and
will not find so.

`awarded_lot` holds **one** lot. This award covers two, so there is no single
value that would be true of it. Writing `Lot 1 and Lot 3` is the obvious
mistake, and the importer refuses it: the award gate requires `awarded_lot` to
be one of the bid's own `lot_numbers`, and that string is not one of them. The
gate caught this record on the first import, which is the gate doing its job.

The same gate accepts this record without `awarded_lot` at all, because the
award rule is `award_date` **and** (`awarded_value` or `awarded_lot`) — either
one is enough. `awarded_value` is 910000 INR, and it is the split across the two
instruments that records which lots were won:

| Contract | Lot | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CON-002` | Lot 1 | 560000 INR |
| `CON-003` | Lot 3 | 350000 INR |
| | | **910000 INR** |

The two values add to the awarded value exactly. So the lot split is not lost by
leaving the single-lot field empty — it is recorded once per contract, which is
where a reader asking "which lot did we win?" will look.

This is the strongest argument for the per-lot contract design. A field that can
hold only one lot cannot describe an award of two lots, so the information has
to live on the instruments themselves.

## The split is visible in the scores

`technical_score` 78 against a maximum of 100, and `financial_score` 58.5, on the
notice's demonstration weighting of 40 percent technical and 60 percent price. The
company scored highest technically on the installation lots, which is where the
notice said experience with site work would be assessed, and lost on price. It won
anyway because the demonstration opening weighted the site-experience criterion
heavily for those two lots.

The losing bid on the same lots scored 62 and 55.5. Nothing here is asserted
without a number behind it.

## An incomplete document list, on purpose

`completed_documents` has two entries and `required_documents` has three. The
demonstration eligibility certificate for Lot 3 is missing, which is recorded
plainly rather than quietly completed.

That is the honest state: the certificate expired before the opening and the
buyer accepted the bid in writing anyway. `eligibility_status` is therefore
`Potentially eligible` and not `Eligible—verified`, because Phase 1's evidence
gate requires a verified claim to carry its evidence and a reviewer, and this
claim does not have both. A record that said `Eligible—verified` here would be
claiming a verification that never happened.

The award was genuinely competitive, so `contract_basis` stays blank for the same
reason it is blank on `BID-004`. On the two contract records this bid produces,
`bid` is filled in and the basis is not: the bid is the authority on how the work
was won, and restating it on each contract would duplicate it twice over.

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL CONTRACT.**
> No contract was signed, performed, or awarded to produce this record.

## The ordinary case: a contract with a bid behind it

This is what a contract record looks like when a competitive bid won the work. The
chain is complete and each link is filled in:

`RFB-002` → `BID-004` → **this record** → `COMP-003`

`bid` is filled in, so `contract_basis` is blank. That pairing is not an oversight.
The bid already records that this award was genuinely competitive, with two
demonstration bids on this lot, and repeating `Awarded after competitive bid` here
would duplicate a fact that is already recorded and could later disagree with it.

`contract_basis` is for the other case: an award with no competing bid behind it.
`CON-004` and `CON-005` are those records.

## The award date is on the bid, not here

The bid was awarded on 2026-09-10. That date is not repeated anywhere on this
record, and there is no `award_date` field to repeat it in.

The reasoning is worth stating because it looks like an omission until you have
seen the alternative. There was a previous design in which the contract carried an
award date too. It was removed, because a date that exists in two places is a date
that will eventually disagree in two places — and the disagreement would be
invisible until someone read both records and noticed. One owner per fact:

| Fact | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| The work was won on 2026-09-10 | `BID-004.award_date` |
| The work was won at 640000 INR | `BID-004.awarded_value` |
| We signed on 2026-09-18 | `contract_signature_date` |
| Obligations run 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30 | `contract_start_date` / `contract_end_date` |

The importer enforces this: a Contract record carrying an award date of any name
fails validation.

## Four statuses, four clocks

| Field | Value | Why it is here and not earlier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contract_status` | `Active` | Signed and running |
| `acceptance_status` | `Pending` | Nothing delivered yet, so nothing to accept |
| `payment_status` | `Not started` | First milestone not yet invoiced |
| `performance_security_status` | `Submitted` | Security posted, not yet released |

Nothing here contradicts anything else, and none of the four could be derived from
another. `Active` does not imply `Not started` — work can be active and already
paid — which is exactly why they are separate fields rather than one status column.

## Money, twice over, in the same currency

`contract_value` is 640000 INR, matching the bid's `awarded_value` of the same
amount. The 64000 INR performance guarantee is a tenth of that, which is the
demonstration rate stated on the notice.

Both amounts carry their own currency field and neither is ever added to an amount
in another currency. The guarantee is money we might have to pay, not money we
expect, and the two are recorded separately for that reason as well as for
bookkeeping: a single "value" column would have to choose between them.

## Acceptance is pending, and the date is blank

`acceptance_status` is `Pending` and `acceptance_date` is blank. Those go together
at the start of a contract's life — the buyer has not accepted anything, so there is
no date to record. The blank is the honest value, not a gap.

> **FICTIONAL DEMONSTRATION RECORD — NOT A REAL CONTRACT.**
> No contract was signed, performed, or awarded to produce this record.

## A contract with no bid, and why that is allowed

`bid` is blank on this record. That is the whole point of it.

Most contracts descend from a competitive bid, so filling `bid` in is the ordinary
case — `CON-001`, `CON-002`, and `CON-003` all do it. A single-source award is
different: there was no competition, so there is no bid record to point at. Not a
missing bid record. No bid, by construction.

`RFB-003` was published as a single-source procurement. `BID-003` is the record of
this company assessing it, and its decision was `No bid` — with the reasoning
recorded rather than left blank, because Phase 1 treats that rationale as the
durable institutional value of a declined opportunity. The reasoning states that a
single-source award to the incumbent licence holder offers no competitive route.

So the chain has a deliberate gap in it:

`RFB-003` → *(no bid)* → **this record** → `COMP-001`

## `contract_basis` is doing the work a link cannot

Because `bid` is blank, `contract_basis` is required, and here it reads `Single
source`. The importer enforces the pairing in both directions:

| `bid` | `contract_basis` | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filled | blank | Fine — competitive award, the bid explains it |
| blank | filled | Fine — this record |
| blank | blank | **Rejected** — nothing records why there was no competition |
| filled | filled | Allowed, but must agree with the bid's own value |

The fourth row is worth noting. `contract_basis` is shared with Bid, and a contract
carrying it while also pointing at a bid is restating its bid rather than
contradicting it — so the importer checks the two agree instead of banning the
combination.

`notice` and `company` stay required even here. A single-source award still descends
from a published notice, so a contract with no notice behind it would not be a
procurement record at all.

## Higher retention, longer term

`retention_percentage` is 10 here against 5 on the two `RFB-002` contracts, and the
warranty runs six months past the end date. Nothing in the record says why, because
the demonstration notice does not state why either.

That is deliberate. The vault does not invent commercial terms, and a reader
comparing two records should be able to see that they differ without the vault
claiming to know the reason. A fabricated explanation would be worse than an
unexplained difference.

## Part paid against an unaccepted contract

`payment_status: Partially paid` with 500000 INR received against 1250000 INR, while
`acceptance_status` is still `Pending`. The demonstration terms evidently permit
payment against milestones rather than against acceptance.

This is the clearest case for why acceptance and payment are separate fields. Read
as one status, "Active, part paid" alongside an unaccepted contract looks like an
inconsistency to be corrected. Read as two independent facts, it is a contract
being paid on schedule against milestones, with the buyer's formal sign-off still
outstanding — an entirely ordinary state, and one that a single status column would
have had to misrepresent in one direction or the other.

| `contract_value` | `415000` |

Everything else is blank: no signature date, no start or end date, no scope, no
milestones, no guarantee amount, no acceptance date, nothing received.

**None of those blanks is an error, and none may be filled with a guess.** The
award has been made; nobody has signed, mobilised, delivered, or been paid. A
signature date of the award date would be a lie, and a start date invented from the
notice's closing date would be worse. A blank means "not established", and this
record is what that looks like when a type's optional fields are left honestly
alone.

`performance_guarantee_required: false` with
`performance_security_status: Not required` is a real answer rather than a blank
one — the buyer demands no security, so the two agree and the currency fields stay
empty because there is no amount to label. Note the boolean is still filled: it is
optional as a field but cannot be blank, because "the buyer requires no guarantee"
and "we do not know whether one is required" are different situations.

## A second instrument from one notice, still with no bid

This contract descends from `RFB-001` and has no bid either — `contract_basis` reads
`Direct award`. `RFB-001` is the demonstration framework notice, and this record
represents a works order called off under it.

`CON-004` is also a no-bid contract on a single-source procurement. Two different
reasons for the same blank link, which is the point: `bid` being empty does not mean
one specific thing, and `contract_basis` is what distinguishes them.

## The only USD record, and why nothing totals it

`contract_value` is 415000 **USD**. Every other amount in the vault is INR.

This is why the rule exists. It would be easy to write a "total contract value"
metric on the contracts page, and with these five records such a total would
produce a confidently wrong number. The importer checks that no contract field name
invites a total and that no contract record carries a computed aggregate, and this
record is the reason that check is not theoretical.

Any portfolio figure must group by currency first. `415000 USD` and `640000 INR`
are not numbers that can be added, and a system that let them be added would produce
a total that means nothing while looking authoritative.
